notes_for_editor: Very thin: the sources give a county, coordinates, an elevation and a GFC number, and nothing on build date, builder, staffing, fires, status or access. The name 'air line' is the list compiler's label (see the note on towers 73 and above), so it is not evidence of an official name. The Wikipedia community of the same name is a separate place (a post office from 1856 to 1907, cited to a postal history site that was not read); no source links it to the tower. Two WebSearch passes and the Hart County fire history found nothing on a tower, and no Hart County tower record exists in the cache. The story is about 130 words. Verification 2026-10-21: the 'covering 203 towers' sentence now says the gfc-nnn numbers come from an older list that described 203 towers, rather than implying every GFC number (for example 920) comes from a 203-tower list. The 73-and-above naming note applies because GA321 is above 73. Consider holding it for a Georgia Forestry Commission answer on whether GFC 920 still stands.
